summary: All 5 FEATs completed successfully with comprehensive test coverage (621 tests passing). Security fixes (command injection, password validation), performance optimizations (indexes, N+1 queries), and code quality improvements (error handling standardization, cache tests) all meet acceptance criteria. PHPStan and Pint checks pass. Four minor concerns identified but non-blocking: Windows path escaping edge cases, non-blocking password validation, database driver support limited to MySQL/SQLite, and restricted special character set in password regex.

findings.issue: escapeshellarg() wraps paths in single quotes which may break icacls command syntax on Windows with paths containing spaces or special characters
findings.suggestion: Test with various Windows path edge cases or use proc_open() with argument arrays to bypass shell interpretation entirely

findings.issue: Weak passwords log a warning but seeder continues execution, allowing deployment with insecure credentials if forced password reset is skipped
findings.suggestion: Consider throwing an exception in production when weak passwords are detected, or document this as an intentional gap with required first-login password change

findings.issue: indexExists() only supports MySQL and SQLite via raw SQL queries. PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and other drivers return false and skip index creation silently
findings.suggestion: Add support for PostgreSQL and SQL Server system tables, or document the MySQL/SQLite limitation in the migration

findings.issue: Password regex pattern only allows @$!%*?&# as special characters, excluding valid characters like ^~+-_=[]{}|;:,.<>
findings.suggestion: Expand the special character set to include common password characters or document the restriction

approved_sections: FEAT-001: Security fixes (command injection with escapeshellarg, password validation with logging)
FEAT-002: Database indexes (conditional creation, composite index on comments)
FEAT-003: N+1 query fix (comment nesting eager loading)
FEAT-004: Error handling standardization (RespondsWithError trait applied to 4 controllers)
FEAT-005: Cache invalidation tests (18 tests, all passing, verified existing behavior)
Code quality: PHPStan passes, Pint formatting passes
Test coverage: 621 tests passing, new cache invalidation tests comprehensive
Laravel best practices: Observer pattern, service layer, trait-based error handling
No breaking changes to existing functionality
